args: Analyze the root cause and safest minimal patch for the out-of-bounds read in DnsLayer::parseResources() in PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsLayer.cpp. Specifically explain how encoded DNS name length is represented by DnsResource/DnsQuery, whether getNameLength() itself is bounds-safe, and how to validate the name, the 10-byte fixed resource-record header, RDLENGTH, and RDATA before calling DnsResource::getSize(). Identify existing helper APIs or analogous validation elsewhere in this codebase.

The sanitizer reports a 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow in PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsResource.cpp DnsResource::getDataLength(), called by inline getSize() from PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsLayer.cpp parseResources(). The attacker controls DNS answer/authority/additional counts and supplies a truncated record near packet end. Current logic reportedly constructs a DnsResource at offsetInPacket and calls getSize() before checking offsetInPacket > m_DataLen. I have not edited anything yet. The desired patch must be confined to C/C++ under PcapPlusPlus, preserve valid DNS parsing, and reject/stop parsing malformed truncated resources before any unsafe access.
